Plot a Network Chart following WJP style guidelines

Source: R/networkChart.R
wjp_network.Rd

wjp_network() takes a data frame of nodes (with their coordinates) and a data frame of weighted edges, and returns a ggplot object with a network chart following WJP style guidelines: round nodes shaded by their centrality (or by a value), edges whose width and opacity grow with their weight, and the name and value of each node printed inside it.

Usage

wjp_network(
  nodes,
  edges,
  x = "x",
  y = "y",
  labels = "label",
  value_labels = NULL,
  weight = "weight",
  node_radius = NULL,
  fill = c("centrality", "value"),
  colors = c("#A8A8C8", "#39396B"),
  edge_color = "#5D6D7E",
  edge_width = c(0.6, 3.2),
  edge_alpha = c(0.2, 0.85),
  ids = NULL,
  from = "from",
  to = "to",
  node_value = NULL,
  edge_gamma = 0.8,
  border_color = "#2C3E50",
  border_width = 0.9,
  label_size = 8,
  label_fontface = "bold",
  label_colour = "auto",
  label_lineheight = 1.15,
  label_wrap = NULL,
  padding = NULL,
  ptheme = WJP_theme()
)

Arguments

nodes

Data frame with one row per node.

edges

Data frame with one row per edge.

x, y

Strings. Columns of nodes with the coordinates of the nodes. Default is "x" and "y".

labels

String. Column of nodes with the names drawn in the nodes. Default is "label".

value_labels

String. Column of nodes with a second line of text (e.g., "(40%)"). Default is NULL.

weight

String. Column of edges with the weight of each edge. Default is "weight".

node_radius

Numeric. Radius of the nodes, in units of the layout. Default is NULL (6.5% of the largest side of the layout).

fill

String. "centrality" (default) or "value". See Details.

colors

Character vector of length 2 with the fill of the least and the most central (or valued) nodes. Default is c("#A8A8C8", "#39396B").

edge_color

String. Color of the edges. Default is "#5D6D7E".

edge_width

Width of the edges, in points: a range c(min, max), a single value, or a function of the weights. Default is c(0.6, 3.2).

edge_alpha

Opacity of the edges: a range c(min, max), a single value, or a function of the weights. Default is c(0.2, 0.85).

ids

String. Column of nodes with the node identifiers used in edges. Default is NULL (labels).

from, to

Strings. Columns of edges with the identifiers of the two nodes of each edge. Default is "from" and "to".

node_value

String. Column of nodes used by fill = "value". Default is NULL.

edge_gamma

Numeric. Exponent applied to the rescaled weights for the edge widths. Default is 0.8.

border_color

String. Color of the node outlines. Default is "#2C3E50"; NA removes them.

border_width

Numeric. Width of the node outlines, in points. Default is 0.9.

label_size

Numeric. Size of the node text, in points. Default is 8.

label_fontface

String. Font face of the node text. Default is "bold". Weight faces such as "semibold" are accepted (see wjp_fonts()).

label_colour

String. Color of the node text, or "auto" (default) for white text on dark nodes and dark text on light nodes.

label_lineheight

Numeric. Distance between the lines of the node text, in ems. Default is 1.15.

label_wrap

Numeric. Maximum number of characters per line of the node names. Default is NULL (no wrapping).

padding

Numeric. Space around the nodes, in units of the layout. Default is NULL (1.17 times node_radius).

ptheme

ggplot theme to apply. Default is WJP_theme().

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

The node layout is taken as given (x, y): compute it beforehand with any graph layout algorithm. The chart keeps the aspect ratio of the layout (one unit of x equals one unit of y) and spans the box of the nodes plus padding, so a figure saved with the same aspect ratio has no empty margins.

Node fill. With fill = "centrality", each node is shaded by the sum of the weights of its edges (its strength), rescaled to 0-1 and mixed between the two colors in RGB space. With fill = "value", the column node_value is used instead. The text of each node is white on dark fills and dark on light fills (label_colour = "auto").

Edges. The weight of each edge is rescaled to 0-1 (t). Its width is edge_width[1] + (edge_width[2] - edge_width[1]) * t^edge_gamma points and its opacity edge_alpha[1] + (edge_alpha[2] - edge_alpha[1]) * t. Both edge_width and edge_alpha also accept a single value or a function of the raw weights. Edges are drawn from the thinnest to the thickest, below the nodes.

Node names can contain line breaks ("\n"); use ids when the names drawn differ from the identifiers used in edges.

Examples

# Always load the WJP fonts
wjp_fonts()

# Co-occurrence of problems (fictional data)
nodes <- data.frame(
  problem = c("Consumer", "Housing", "Family", "Money & Debt", "Employment"),
  share   = c("(40%)", "(10%)", "(18%)", "(22%)", "(19%)"),
  x       = c(1.0, 0.3, 0.9, 0.3, 0.1),
  y       = c(0.2, 0.6, 0.5, 0.9, 0.3)
)
nodes$name <- c("Consumer", "Housing", "Family", "Money &\nDebt", "Employment")
edges <- data.frame(
  from = c("Consumer", "Consumer", "Housing", "Family", "Money & Debt", "Housing"),
  to   = c("Family", "Money & Debt", "Money & Debt", "Employment", "Employment", "Family"),
  lift = c(1.7, 2.1, 2.8, 1.9, 2.4, 2.2)
)

wjp_network(
  nodes, edges,
  labels       = "name",
  ids          = "problem",
  value_labels = "share",
  weight       = "lift"
)
